lessons.title: Non-Fiction: Our Amazing Bodies
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to retrieve facts about the human body from a non-fiction text.
success_criteria: I can find a fact about the body.
I can answer a question using the text.
lessons.starter_activity: Discuss what children already know about their bodies.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model reading a simple non-fiction text about the human body.
lessons.independent_task: Children read an extract and answer retrieval questions about the body.
resources_needed: Non-fiction text about the human body
key_questions: What does this body part do?
Where did you find that fact?

differentiation.greater_depth: Answer in full sentences using text evidence

lessons.assessment_notes: Note non-fiction retrieval skill — evidence for ENG.R2.
lessons.plenary: Recap facts found about the body.
lessons.home_link: Find a fact about the body in a book at home.

lessons.title: Counting Body Parts
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to count body parts and small groups accurately to 20.
success_criteria: I can count body parts.
I can write the numeral.
lessons.starter_activity: Count eyes, ears, fingers as a class.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model counting body parts (individual and in groups, e.g. fingers on both hands) recording numerals.
lessons.independent_task: Children count body parts (own and in pictures) up to 20, recording numerals.
key_questions: How many fingers do you have?
How many toes altogether in the class?

differentiation.greater_depth: Count to 20+ and compare totals across pairs

lessons.assessment_notes: Record counting accuracy to 20 — evidence for MATHS.N1.
lessons.home_link: Count body parts together at home.

lessons.title: Naming Body Parts (Recap and Extend)
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to name a wider range of body parts than in EYFS.
success_criteria: I can name 8+ body parts.
I can label a body diagram.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap body parts known from EYFS.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Extend body part vocabulary (knee, elbow, wrist, ankle, shoulder, chin, forehead).
lessons.independent_task: Children label a detailed body outline diagram with as many parts as they can.
key_questions: What is this part called?
Can you point to your ankle?

differentiation.support: Word bank with matching pictures provided

lessons.assessment_notes: Note vocabulary range and labelling accuracy, an extension of EYFS learning — evidence for SCI.ANI.
lessons.home_link: Name body parts together while getting ready for bed.

lessons.title: Writing About What My Body Can Do
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to write sentences describing what their body can do.
success_criteria: I can write what my body can do.
I can use a capital letter and full stop.
lessons.starter_activity: Discuss things bodies can do (run, jump, clap).
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model writing sentences starting 'My body can...'
lessons.independent_task: Children write 2-3 sentences about what their body can do.
key_questions: What can your body do?
Can you write a sentence about it?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note sentence writing progress — evidence for ENG.W2/W3.
lessons.home_link: Tell your family something amazing your body can do.

lessons.title: Measuring Height
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to measure and compare height using non-standard units.
success_criteria: I can measure height using cubes.
I can compare two heights.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap comparing length/height from earlier weeks.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model measuring height using stacked cubes or a paper strip.
lessons.independent_task: Children measure their own height (or a partner's, sensitively) using non-standard units, comparing results.
key_questions: How many cubes tall are you?
Who is taller?
lessons.assessment_notes: Record height measurement skill sensitively — evidence for MATHS.MEA.
lessons.home_link: Measure your height against a family member's (sensitively).

lessons.title: My Five Senses (Recap and Extend)
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to name the five senses and their associated body part.
success_criteria: I can name the five senses.
I can match each to a body part.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap the five senses from EYFS.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Recap and extend understanding of the five senses and their body parts.
lessons.independent_task: Children match each sense to its body part and give an example of using it.
key_questions: Which body part helps you hear?
Can you give an example of using taste?

differentiation.greater_depth: Give a detailed example for each sense

lessons.assessment_notes: Note extension of EYFS senses learning — evidence for SCI.ANI.
lessons.plenary: Recap the five senses and body parts.
lessons.home_link: Play a senses guessing game at home.

lessons.title: Phonics: Reading Body-Themed Words
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to blend and read body-themed words.
success_criteria: I can blend and read body words.
I can read a sentence about the body.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Introduce/reinforce a grapheme, blending body-themed words (e.g. 'hand', 'leg', 'chin').
lessons.independent_task: Children read body-themed word and sentence cards.
key_questions: Can you blend this word?
Can you read this sentence?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note phonics application — evidence for ENG.R1.
lessons.plenary: Celebrate reading progress with a themed reading game.
lessons.home_link: Practise reading body words over the week.

lessons.title: Measuring Hand Span
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to measure objects using their own hand span.
success_criteria: I can measure using my hand span.
I can compare my measurement to a friend's.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model measuring an object using hand spans, discussing why everyone's measurement might differ.
lessons.independent_task: Children measure classroom objects using hand spans, comparing results with a partner.
key_questions: How many hand spans long is this?
Why might your answer be different from your partner's?

differentiation.greater_depth: Measure 4+ objects and discuss measurement variation

lessons.assessment_notes: Note early understanding of measurement variability with non-standard units — evidence for MATHS.MEA.
lessons.plenary: Recap hand span measurements and discuss standard units briefly.
lessons.home_link: Measure something at home using your hand span.

lessons.title: Healthy Eating for Our Bodies
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to describe why healthy eating is important for our bodies.
success_criteria: I can name a healthy food.
I can say why it's good for us.
lessons.starter_activity: Discuss favourite foods and whether they're healthy.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Discuss the importance of healthy eating for growth and energy, using simple food groups.
lessons.independent_task: Children sort food picture cards into healthy/occasional, recording reasoning.
key_questions: Why is this food healthy?
What does it help our bodies do?

differentiation.support: Sort with adult support, obvious examples
differentiation.greater_depth: Explain reasoning for less obvious examples

lessons.assessment_notes: Note understanding of healthy eating and body needs — evidence for SCI.ANI.
lessons.home_link: Talk about a healthy meal you could have today.

lessons.title: Exercise and My Body Discussion
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to discuss why exercise is good for the body.
success_criteria: I can say why exercise is good for us.
I can name an exercise I enjoy.
lessons.starter_activity: Do a short physical warm-up (jumping jacks, stretches).
lessons.main_teaching_input: Discuss why exercise is good for the body (strong muscles, healthy heart, feeling good).
lessons.independent_task: Children discuss and record their favourite exercise and why it's good for their body.
key_questions: Why is exercise good for us?
What exercise do you enjoy?

differentiation.greater_depth: Explain the body benefit in more detail

lessons.assessment_notes: Note understanding of exercise benefits — evidence for ENG.SL1/SCI.ANI.
lessons.home_link: Do a favourite exercise with your family.

lessons.title: Body-Themed Word Problems
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to solve addition/subtraction word problems using a body context.
success_criteria: I can solve an addition problem.
I can solve a subtraction problem.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model solving word problems using a body context (e.g. counting fingers/toes).
lessons.independent_task: Children solve body-themed word problems, showing working.
key_questions: How many fingers altogether?
How many are left?
lessons.assessment_notes: Record word problem solving skill — evidence for MATHS.N2.
lessons.home_link: Make up a body-themed word problem for your family.

lessons.title: Hygiene: Keeping Our Bodies Clean
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to describe why hygiene routines keep us healthy.
success_criteria: I can name a hygiene routine.
I can say why it's important.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Discuss hygiene routines (washing hands, brushing teeth, bathing) and why they matter.
lessons.independent_task: Children sequence a hygiene routine (e.g. handwashing steps) and explain its importance.
key_questions: Why do we wash our hands?
What happens if we don't?

differentiation.greater_depth: Explain the science of germs simply

lessons.assessment_notes: Note understanding of hygiene and health — evidence for SCI.ANI.
lessons.home_link: Practise a hygiene routine carefully tonight.

lessons.title: Human Body Quiz: Reading Comprehension
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to answer comprehension questions about the human body.
success_criteria: I can answer a retrieval question.
I can answer an inference question.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Read a summary passage about the human body, modelling retrieval and inference questions.
lessons.independent_task: Children answer a mix of retrieval and inference questions about the passage.
key_questions: What does exercise do for our bodies?
Why is healthy eating important?

differentiation.support: Answer retrieval questions with text pointing

lessons.assessment_notes: Note comprehension progress — evidence for ENG.R2.
lessons.home_link: Quiz your family on body facts you learned.

lessons.title: Maths Review: Measuring and Word Problems
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to apply measuring and word problem skills learned this week.
success_criteria: I can measure using non-standard units.
I can solve a word problem.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Quick recap of measuring height/hand span and word problems.
lessons.independent_task: Children rotate through 2 stations: measuring, word problems.
key_questions: How did you measure this?
How did you solve this problem?
lessons.assessment_notes: Summarise week 24 maths observations for each child — evidence for MATHS.MEA/N2.
lessons.plenary: Class recap game combining both skills.

lessons.title: Human Body Topic Recap and Celebration
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to summarise key learning about the human body, health and hygiene.
success_criteria: I can name a body part and its job.
I can name a healthy habit.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Quick recap quiz format covering body parts, senses, healthy eating, exercise, and hygiene.
lessons.independent_task: Children complete a review worksheet and contribute to a class 'Amazing Bodies' display.
key_questions: What have we learned about our bodies?
What was most interesting?

differentiation.support: Word bank and picture support provided

lessons.assessment_notes: Note human body/health understanding progress — evidence for SCI.ANI.
lessons.plenary: Celebrate the week's human body learning.
lessons.home_link: Share what you learned about your body with your family.
